newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends edge higher on dollar unwinding.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends edge higher on dollar unwinding.

text.p: The won closed slightly higher against the dollar on Wednesday due to dollar unwinding and the central bank's dollar sales, dealers said.
But the dollar's rise against the yen on world markets briefly pushed the won to an intraday low of 860.00, they said.
"Views prevail that the won's fall will be limited to the 860.00 level for the time being," said a domestic bank dealer.
The won closed at 859.40 after opening at 859.50. It touched a high of 859.00.
Dealers said expectations of tightening liquidity before the Lunar New Year holidays next week prompted dollar sales.
The won's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 859.60 on Thursday, compared with Wednesday's 857.50.
Dealers said the Bank of Korea sold dollars in early morning trading at around 859.60 won to slow the won's fall.
"Dollar positions with banks remained high because they had been reluctant to sell dollars. But now they seem to think the dollar was overbought," said a foreign bank dealer.
Dealers forecast trading would range from 857.00-857.70 to 859.50-859.70 on Thursday.
